subject: Security exhibit: evidence cadence, pen-test scope, and order-form redlines
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clarionhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Morris <leah.morris@clarionhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit questions and timing

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward the order form I need to confirm a few items for our InfoSec and procurement teams so we can get internal approvals:

- Can you confirm the SOC 2 evidence cadence (what artifacts we get and how often)?
- For pen tests: do you allow customer-run tests, or only third-party tests through your scheduled window? If customer-run, what are the guardrails (IP ranges, scoping rules, coordination lead)?
- We also need suggested redline language for the security exhibit and any sample MSA/order form clauses so our legal team can speed review.

We'd like to get these finalized before our procurement deadline (end of this month). Happy to jump on a short call — Leah (cc'd) will coordinate.

Best,
Sam Patel
Head of Security Operations
Clarion Health

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions and timing

Thanks Sam — good questions. I pulled together the short answers and attached a brief evidence map and SOC 2 summary for your legal/compliance review. Key points below; happy to call if you want to run through.

Quick answers:
- SOC 2 evidence cadence: we provide quarterly snapshots of SOC 2 attestation artifacts plus a rolling set of operational artifacts (config exports, backup verification, change logs) on request with a 3-business-day SLA for routine requests. See attached evidence-map.xlsx.
- Pen test approach: Redwood supports both vendor-driven and customer-initiated tests. We run a scheduled window (customer books a 2-week window with our ops team) for tests we coordinate; for customer-run/third-party tests we require a pre-test scoping form, a PVN (privileged inspection notification) and a mutually agreed blast-radius document. We do not permit destructive testing or any lateral network access outside agreed targets.
- Redlines/example language: attached security_exhibit_redline_draft.docx — Karthik has proposed alternative language for bounded inspection and pen-test assertions.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to provide the legal redline (cc'd) — target EOD tomorrow.
2) I'll schedule a 30-min technical ops call with your team and CyberAssure to sketch the pen-test window and scoping checklist (Laura to own scheduling).
3) Vanessa will surface any dedicated capacity/SLA carveouts that affect the order form pricing.

If that works I'll follow up with a consolidated calendar invite.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions and timing

I reviewed the initial exhibit and drafted a targeted redline that narrows the inspection rights and clarifies pen-test assertions. Major changes I recommend:

- Bounded inspection: change open-ended "inspection access" to "time-boxed, scoped inspection" with maximum 5 business days of privileged access per rolling 12-month period unless otherwise agreed.
- Pen test custody: define that tests must be pre-authorized, provide a named lead, and supply test artifacts within 10 business days; Redwood retains the right to suspend tests if agreed blast-radius clauses are breached.
- Evidence requests: routine evidence (logs/configs) will be provided within 3 business days; escalated requests (forensics, deep config dumps) require a legal/subpoena or an agreed escalation playbook and may incur professional-services fees.

I attached security_exhibit_redline_draft.docx — Sam/Leah, please scan the alternate wording and flag any non-starters. If we can get high-level agreement on bounded inspection and pen-test assertions, we can model the language into the order form (pricing carveouts will be needed if you want extended privileged windows).

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions and timing

Thanks Karthik — quick responses from our side after a legal/compliance skim:

- The 5-business-day privileged access cap is reasonable but we need clarity on what counts as "privileged access" (console admin vs. read-only exports). Can you enumerate typical access types in the exhibit?
- For pen tests: Clarion prefers to run a third-party test (we have an approved vendor, CyberAssure) during the window. They will require remote network testing and web-app assessments. Can you confirm Redwood's stance on remote external scanning and whether authenticated scans are permitted?
- On evidence SLAs: 3-business-day turnaround for routine items is OK. For escalations, can you commit to a named lead and SLA for turnaround (we suggested 15 business days for deep-dive artifacts)?
- Also — procurement asked us to track DocuSign status. The order form link shows draft; can your sales ops point-of-contact confirm any expected pricing changes if we request extended inspection windows?

We can take the redline offline with Karthik but would like to surface these clarifications before the procurement deadline.

Best,
Leah Morris
Sr. Procurement Manager
Clarion Health

Thanks all — quick consolidated update and actions so we have a single source of truth: 

Decisions/confirmations:
- Privileged access types: we'll enumerate three tiers in the exhibit: (1) Read-only exports (config/logs) — no console access; (2) Authenticated scan rights (test accounts with limited privileges); (3) Time-boxed console access (admin) — only by exception and only during a mutually agreed 1–2 hour session. The 5-business-day cap applies to cumulative admin-level access per 12 months.
- Authenticated scans: allowed within the scheduled 2-week window using test accounts; lateral/malicious activity outside scoped targets is prohibited. Remote external network scanning (non-authenticated) is allowed against public endpoints only.
- Evidence SLAs: routine requests — 3 business days; deep-dive forensics — target 15 business days with an identified Redwood lead (Laura Bennett — cc).

Immediate actions (owners):
- Karthik: finalize the redline with the three-tier access enum and return to Leah/Sam by EOD Mon (2025-06-23).
- Laura: schedule the ops call w/ CyberAssure and Clarion for week of 6/30; prepare contact info for Redwood test accounts.
- Vanessa: provide pricing delta for a 5-business-day privileged window vs. extended window (deliverable 6/24).
- Irene: I'll consolidate the final exhibit + order form note and upload a new draft to DocuSign (link below) once redline approved.

DocuSign/order-form (draft): https://www.docusign.com/Clarion-OrderForm-8392
